Software Engineer (Target Tracking) - ATL / Hybrid / Cherry Hill NJ
Cherry Hill, NJ
Full-time
Hybrid
Entry Level
$75K/yr - $143K/yr
Lockheed Martin is seeking a junior Software Engineer for its Advanced Technology Laboratories. The role develops, tests, and evaluates algorithms and software for multi-target tracking, sensor fusion, and related sensing applications, while supporting research and technical demonstrations.

Responsibilities
Developing, testing, and evaluating Python-based algorithms and software for multi-target tracking, localization, state estimation, and sensor/data fusion
Applying filtering, inference, data-association, and signal-processing techniques to recorded and simulated sensor data
Building simulation environments, data-processing pipelines, analysis tools, and performance-evaluation workflows for complex sensing applications
Integrating prototype algorithms into scalable, maintainable software and larger sensor-system architectures, including CI/CD and DevSecOps practices
Analyzing, debugging, and optimizing tracking software and data-engineering workflows for large-scale sensor-processing and machine-learning data sets
Collaborating with researchers, engineers, and domain experts to advance technical solutions, conduct peer reviews, and document designs and results
Supporting research, customer-focused technical solutions, technical briefings, and proof-of-concept demonstrations for emerging tracking challenges

Required
Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or a closely related field
Demonstrated ability developing and testing Python software for scientific, technical, or algorithmic applications
Strong foundation in probability and statistics, linear algebra, and estimation methods, with familiarity or practical experience in signal processing, state estimation, target tracking, or Kalman filtering
Ability to analyze data, develop and evaluate algorithms, and communicate technical results clearly
Strong collaboration and communication skills and proven ability to work effectively in multi‑disciplinary teams
US Citizenship with eligibility for a US government security clearance is required
Preferred
Advanced degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or a closely related field
Active Secret Clearance or higher
Experience with localization and inference methods from sensor data such as Kalman filters, unscented transforms, and particle filters
Research into frontiers of multi-target tracking using random Finite Sets, including Labeled Multi-Bernoulli (LMB) filters; data association through Monte Carlo and stochastic algorithms (*e.g.*, Gibbs samplers); extensions to multi-sensor data fusion and sensor control applications
Proficiency building simulation, analysis, and data-processing tools in Python using libraries such as NumPy, SciPy, pandas, pymap3d, and matplotlib
Experience with optimization, digital signal processing (DSP), detection theory, and wireless sensing, or related signal-processing applications
Familiarity with collaborative software-development practices, including Git-based version control, automated testing, and CI/CD pipelines
Experience transitioning algorithms to real-time, including porting performance-critical components to C++ or Rust and interfacing with external systems through pub-sub messaging frameworks
Experience working research projects on state‑of‑the‑art technologies (e.g., Counter UAS, next‑gen electronic support)
Understanding of primary mission areas: Electronic Warfare (EW) and Electronic Support Measures (ESM)
Experience with radar and other sensing systems
